title: Alcaraz Smiles After 3:34am Loss: 'I Suffered, But I Enjoyed'
summary:
Most people would be grumpy after losing a tennis match at 3:34 in the morning. But Carlos Alcaraz smiled.

Alcaraz, a 23-year-old tennis champion from Spain, lost to Ben Shelton at the US Open. The match lasted four hours and 28 minutes and ended at 3:34am—the latest finish in the tournament's history. But as Alcaraz walked through the tunnel, he had a huge grin on his face.

Why? Because he had been away from tennis for over five months with a wrist injury. He missed the French Open and Wimbledon. He didn't even know if he could play in New York until a week before.

"I suffered, but I enjoyed, and that's why I smiled," he said. "I missed that feeling."

Alcaraz thinks matches shouldn't go so late. "I would like to change the schedule a little with a maximum finish at 11pm," he said.

Now he's playing for Team Europe in the Laver Cup in London. He says playing with teammates is "a weird feeling but it's beautiful."
why_it_matters: Alcaraz's smile shows that losing doesn't have to ruin your day — coming back to something you love after being hurt can matter even more than winning.

background_read: The US Open is one of the four biggest tennis tournaments in the world and is played every year in New York City, together with the French Open in Paris, Wimbledon in England and the Australian Open.
Carlos Alcaraz is a Spanish star who became the youngest man ever to reach No. 1 in the world tennis rankings, and he has won several of the sport's biggest titles.
The Laver Cup is a team event named after Rod Laver, a famous Australian tennis player; each year a team of European players takes on a team from the rest of the world.

WHAT: A four-hour-28-minute match that finished at 3:34am — the latest finish in the tournament's history — and Alcaraz's happy reaction to it.
WHERE: The US Open in New York, where he played; he is now with Team Europe at the Laver Cup in London.
WHY: He had been out for over five months with a wrist injury and had missed the French Open and Wimbledon, so simply being able to play again made him happy.
